what_it_proves: UnitedHealth is one of the largest healthcare money-routing platforms.
boundary: Revenue scale does not prove care quality, fair access, or clean cash collection.

what_it_proves: The platform remained profitable despite a difficult reset year.
boundary: Operating earnings do not prove patient outcomes or segment-level cash quality.

what_it_proves: The margin was thin relative to the scale of healthcare dollars routed.
boundary: Net margin does not identify medical-cost trend, reserve quality, or pharmacy transparency.

what_it_proves: Shareholder earnings were visible but pressured.
boundary: Adjusted EPS can exclude costs and does not prove durable access quality.

what_it_proves: Revenue scale remained very large early in the recovery year.
boundary: Quarterly revenue does not prove medical-cost control or patient trust.

what_it_proves: Profitability improved materially from the reset baseline.
boundary: One-quarter operating recovery does not prove structural repair.
Margin recovery can reverse if medical costs, policy pressure, or trust issues worsen.

what_it_proves: Per-share earnings improved in the quarter.
boundary: Adjusted EPS does not prove better care or fair authorization practices.

what_it_proves: The platform maintained very large quarterly revenue.
boundary: Revenue durability still depends on pricing, regulation, membership, and trust.

what_it_proves: Profitability remained strong but below Q1.
boundary: Lower sequential operating earnings show recovery still needs qualification.

what_it_proves: Management raised the full-year adjusted EPS range.
boundary: Guidance is not proof; actual results, medical-cost trend, and cash flow must follow.
Expected OCF does not prove segment cash conversion, payer-to-provider collections, or patient benefit.
